analysis:
The two base_text units (base lines 1380-2230 of ClusterOnboardingFlow.swift) cover the ClusterOnboardingOperations struct and init, the pairing state machine, the console protocol, choice matching, and the start of the driver: run, pairAgain, startOver, readBothMacs, checkLink and allowLocalNetwork.

According to the file_changes map, this region's head-side changes add two members at head lines 1518-1525:
- stopsAsked, an optional count of stops a person asked for.
- serveUnlessStopped, an optional closure documented to check the stop count on the leading Mac under the start lock, so a stop that took the lock first is not undone.

The defaults are nil, which falls back to serve. A later hunk passes stopsBefore: nil into provision at head line 2852.

This is local-only cluster onboarding UX and operator control. It does not touch the threat-model assets for prompts, keys, attestation, authorization or billing (A-001..A-017), or the cache (T-041).

The only security-adjacent aspect is availability and operator-intent integrity (A-018): a stop must not be undone by a concurrent start. The new hook narrows that race. Its real enforcement lives in the live operations (OnboardingLive) and ClusterSetupRecord.stopsAsked, which are not supplied.

Open questions for integration:
- Is the stop count read and checked under the same lock that stop takes?
- Is the nil fallback, which means no stop check against older builds, acceptable?
- Can a remote member Mac over the link increment or reset the counter? Peer Macs are not described in the canonical boundaries, though TB-014/T-062 cover a related peer-Mac trigger concern for gpu-limit.

The base code shows no new privileged action. runAsAdministrator and the sudo handling are pre-existing (base 1445-1447).

No regression was identified in the examined units. The changed head ranges at 2901-3539 are in other batches.
